Definition: from a derivative of τρύω (to wear away; akin to the base of G5134, G5147 and G5176); an orifice, i.e. needle's eye:--eye. Compare G5169.
BiblicalUsage: trymaliá is the ordinary word for an orifice, a needle’s eye. It appears once, in Mark 10:25.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that trymaliá is one of the small details that matter in Scripture.
